en: The *Ratnamālā-stotra* composed by the venerable Ācārya Vanaratna:
[I praise] Lokeśvara, whose mind is moist with stainless emptiness and compassion.

I bow my head to the one whose meaningful speech proclaims the renowned knowledge of the paths, whose body is completely pure and perfected by the knowledge of all things and so forth, and who is graced by the mastery of primordial wisdom. (1)
Since you appear in many manifestations according to the differences among those to be trained— just as the single moon appears in various vessels of water—
you are therefore perceived as being solely intent upon the welfare of others.
Oh, how truly marvelous is the nature of Buddhahood! || 2 ||
O you with a face like the full moon,
the charming son of the god Maheśvara emerged from the region of your forehead for the sake of awakening the people of Śambhu’s realm who were to be disciplined.
You are the Lord, born after the image of the God of gods. || 3 ||
Has this body of yours, endowed with the marks of great auspiciousness, been manifested for the sake of awakening the tender hearts of those to be converted?
For your father has indeed already departed to perform worship of the gods.
I bow my head to the supreme Lord of the Lords of Lokeśvara. || 4 ||
He has emerged from the heart of the Lotus-Handed One for the sake of awakening those who are to be disciplined and the devotees of Viṣṇu;
therefore, Nārāyaṇa himself is indeed the Lord of the World.
Among men, you alone are the supreme and most excellent; there is no other.
For the sake of beholding those who possess devotion offered with respect to the Moon and the Sun,
the Moon and the Sun emerged from the two beautiful eyes of the one who is dark as an elephant, in order to appear upon the earth.
I bow to Him who has destroyed the darkness of the intermediate space.
Indeed, this blessed Sarasvatī has appeared here before you for the awakening of those who possess devotion joined with the discipline of Sarasvatī;
she was brought forth by the foremost son of the Jina.
I bow to him who bestows the fruit desired by those seeking wisdom. || 7 ||
That Sugata, the Lord of the World, who has emerged for the sake of accomplishing the path of letters produced by the winds of those to be trained—
may that supreme deity, the Wind, [grant success] to those born upon this earth.
I bow to him who bestows the fruit of the purpose of the [four] postures. || 8 ||
For the sake of awakening those who were to be converted— those who desired the auspicious path of Varuṇa—
the excellent deity Varuṇa himself suddenly emerged from the bellies of the sons of the Sugata.
I bow to Him who bestows the fruit of the perfection of sovereignty. || 9 ||
Indeed, for the sake of the perfect accomplishment of those who desire the fruits esteemed by those to be trained,
the venerable Earth, renowned as such, issued forth from his preeminent lotus feet.
I perpetually bow down to the peerless Lord of the three worlds. || 10 ||
Though liberated from saṃsāra, he remains perfectly established there out of compassion for the multitude of beings wandering in existence;
may my own state likewise always remain steadfastly so.
Thus I bow to that supreme and most noble-minded one. || 11 ||
With a single sole of his own foot,
he covered the entire extent of the world-system in the intermediate realm,
while the worlds were being consumed by the fierce, blazing fire at the end of the aeon.
By the power of your exhaled breath, he shall find peace.
If one holds one's own index finger to the mouth and moves many hosts of mountains with the threatening gesture of the fingernail,
the waters of the ocean would be entirely drawn out from their depths.
Oh, from where else could such power as this of yours come? || 13 ||
Where indeed is this supreme childhood form, so beautiful to behold with its most tender young moon-like face,
and yet the subduer of the irresistible Māra, which can be endured by me alone?
And where is your prowess, which is supreme and difficult for others to endure? || 14 ||
Ah, this row of people with limbs as dark as collyrium,
with their hair at the tips beautifully curled and thick—
[they appear like] a blazing, flickering fire upon the fuel of afflictions.
Indeed, your stainless [splendor] is perceived like a streak of smoke. 15.
The entire splendor of the ten directions, purified by a mere fragment of your radiance, becomes slender at the end of the dark fortnight;
for it is only at the periphery that it is desired within the dwellings of the moon.
I believe that everything in the radiant universe exists through but a fraction of your splendor. || 16 ||
Who indeed is a kinsman? It is the man or woman who honors the path approved by seekers, and that which leads to the true path.
I bow to the Victor, the sovereign lord of the earth, who is supreme because he has perfected the vows for the sake of others.

I bow to the Victorious One, the sovereign king of the earth, who abides in the state of impermanent nirvāṇa, who is established in and endowed with luminosity, who brings benefit, who has brought all people to peace, and who is auspicious and blissful. 18.

I bow to the Jina, the king of lords of the earth, who is filled with an immeasurable garland of rays, whose family is marked by the lotus held in his own hand, who is intensely devoted to the beauty that follows his passion, and who is the very embodiment of delight. 19.

I pay homage to the Jina, the Lord of the Earth, the Conqueror who has mastered his own realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), who is supreme through his devotion to compassion, who is fully filled with the well-accumulated provisions of merit and wisdom, who is free from conceptual construction, who teaches by means of sound, and who is capable [of liberation]. (20)

I bow to the supreme King of the Lords of the Earth, who possesses hundreds of knowledges regarding suchness and non-duality; who proclaims the Dharma that fulfills both existence and non-existence; and who is devoted to the truth adorned with all that is to be taught. 21.
I bow down with speed to the best of kings upon the earth, who possesses the form of a choice lotus, whose beautiful lotus-eyes extend throughout the world, and who is supremely pure in his essence.

I bow to the supreme king of lords of the earth, who delights in the welfare of others through excellent emanated enjoyments, who is devoted to the stainless Dharma of emptiness, and who is intent on the accomplishments that adorn the sovereign of the earth. (23)

I pay homage to the supreme King of the Lords of the Earth, whose face is like the moon rising from the ocean of the excellent and innate [wisdom], who has eloquently taught the state of liberation for sentient beings, and who is unsurpassed in the characteristics of his marks and ornaments. 24.
The venerable Vanaratnapāda had this jewel-garland for me, Lokeśvara, fashioned;
by whatever merit has been acquired through that, may the world become Samantabhadra. 25.
The Jewel Garland Praise of the Blessed Lord, the Glorious Noble Avalokiteśvara, is complete.
